title: A Minimum-Energy Control Approach for Redundant Mobile Manipulators in Physical Human-Robot Interaction Applications
summary: Research on mobile manipulation systems that physically interact with humans has expanded rapidly in recent years, opening the way to tasks which could not be performed using fixed-base manipulators. Within this context, developing suitable control methodologies is essential since mobile manipulators introduce additional degrees of freedom, making the design of control approaches more challenging and more prone to performance optimization. This paper proposes a control approach for a mobile manipulator, composed of a mobile base equipped with a robotic arm mounted on the top, with the objective of minimizing the overall kinetic energy stored in the whole-body mobile manipulator in physical human-robot interaction applications. The approach is experimentally tested with reference to a peg-in-hole task, and the results demonstrate that the proposed approach reduces the overall kinetic energy stored in the whole-body robotic system and improves the system performance compared with the benchmark method.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a control approach for mobile manipulators that minimizes overall kinetic energy during physical human-robot interaction, demonstrating improved performance in peg-in-hole tasks compared to benchmark methods.
AI.motivation: Mobile manipulation systems for human interaction are growing, but the additional degrees of freedom make control design more challenging and performance optimization more complex than with fixed-base manipulators.
AI.method: A control approach for a mobile manipulator (mobile base with mounted robotic arm) that minimizes the overall kinetic energy stored in the whole-body system during physical human-robot interaction applications.
AI.result: Experimentally tested on a peg-in-hole task, showing the proposed approach reduces overall kinetic energy and improves system performance compared to the benchmark method.
AI.conclusion: The proposed control successfully reduces kinetic energy and enhances performance in human-robot interaction tasks, validating its effectiveness for mobile manipulation systems.

title: Connectivity-Aware Representations for Constrained Motion Planning via Multi-Scale Contrastive Learning
summary: The objective of constrained motion planning is to connect start and goal configurations while satisfying task-specific constraints. Motion planning becomes inefficient or infeasible when the configurations lie in disconnected regions, known as essentially mutually disconnected (EMD) components. Constraints further restrict feasible space to a lower-dimensional submanifold, while redundancy introduces additional complexity because a single end-effector pose admits infinitely many inverse kinematic solutions that may form discrete self-motion manifolds. This paper addresses these challenges by learning a connectivity-aware representation for selecting start and goal configurations prior to planning. Joint configurations are embedded into a latent space through multi-scale manifold learning across neighborhood ranges from local to global, and clustering generates pseudo-labels that supervise a contrastive learning framework. The proposed framework provides a connectivity-aware measure that biases the selection of start and goal configurations in connected regions, avoiding EMDs and yielding higher success rates with reduced planning time. Experiments on various manipulation tasks showed that our method achieves 1.9 times higher success rates and reduces the planning time by a factor of 0.43 compared to baselines.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a connectivity-aware representation learning framework that embeds joint configurations into a latent space using multi-scale manifold learning and contrastive learning. By selecting start and goal configurations from connected regions, the method avoids essentially mutually disconnected (EMD) components, achieving 1.9× higher success rates and 0.43× planning time compared to baselines across manipulation tasks.
AI.motivation: Motion planning faces two critical challenges: (1) configurations lying in disconnected regions (EMD components) make planning inefficient or infeasible; (2) task constraints reduce feasible space to lower-dimensional submanifolds, while robot redundancy introduces complexity through infinite inverse kinematic solutions forming discrete self-motion manifolds. The paper aims to address these challenges by learning a connectivity-aware representation to guide configuration selection prior to planning.
AI.method: The proposed framework learns a connectivity-aware representation through multi-scale manifold learning across neighborhood ranges (local to global), embedding joint configurations into a latent space. Clustering generates pseudo-labels that supervise a contrastive learning framework. This creates a connectivity-aware measure that biases the selection of start and goal configurations toward connected regions, avoiding EMD components and enabling more efficient planning.
AI.result: Experiments on various manipulation tasks demonstrate significant improvements: 1.9 times higher success rates compared to baselines, and planning time reduced by a factor of 0.43 (approximately 43% reduction), validating the effectiveness of the connectivity-aware selection approach.
AI.conclusion: The connectivity-aware representation learning framework successfully addresses the challenges of EMD components, constrained motion planning, and redundancy complexity. By selecting configurations from connected regions, the method yields higher success rates and reduced planning time, demonstrating its practical value for robotic manipulation tasks.

title: SafeGuard ASF: SR Agentic Humanoid Robot System for Autonomous Industrial Safety
summary: The rise of unmanned ``dark factories'' operating without human presence demands autonomous safety systems capable of detecting and responding to multiple hazard types. We present SafeGuard ASF (Agentic Security Fleet), a comprehensive framework deploying humanoid robots for autonomous hazard detection in industrial environments. Our system integrates multi-modal perception (RGB-D imaging), a ReAct-based agentic reasoning framework, and learned locomotion policies on the Unitree G1 humanoid platform. We address three critical hazard scenarios: fire and smoke detection, abnormal temperature monitoring in pipelines, and intruder detection in restricted zones. Our perception pipeline achieves 94.2% mAP for fire or smoke detection with 127ms latency. We train multiple locomotion policies, including dance motion tracking and velocity control, using Unitree RL Lab with PPO, demonstrating stable convergence within 80,000 training iterations. We validate our system in both simulation and real-world environments, demonstrating autonomous patrol, human detection with visual perception, and obstacle avoidance capabilities. The proposed ToolOrchestra action framework enables structured decision-making through perception, reasoning, and actuation tools.

AI.tldr: SafeGuard ASF deploys humanoid robots (Unitree G1) with multi-modal perception (RGB-D), ReAct-based reasoning, and locomotion policies to autonomously detect and respond to fire, temperature anomalies, and intruders in industrial dark factories.
AI.motivation: Dark factories require autonomous safety systems that can detect and respond to multiple hazard types without human presence. Existing solutions lack comprehensive detection capabilities across fire, temperature, and intrusion scenarios.
AI.method: Integrates RGB-D imaging for multi-modal perception, ReAct-based agentic reasoning framework, and learned locomotion policies on Unitree G1 humanoid using Unitree RL Lab and PPO. Implements ToolOrchestra action framework for structured decision-making.
AI.result: Achieves 94.2% mAP for fire/smoke detection with 127ms latency. Multiple locomotion policies converge stably within 80,000 training iterations. Validated in both simulation and real-world environments with autonomous patrol, human detection, and obstacle avoidance capabilities.
AI.conclusion: SafeGuard ASF demonstrates a comprehensive autonomous safety solution for industrial environments, successfully addressing multiple hazard types through integrated perception, reasoning, and action capabilities in real-world dark factory settings.

title: Bayesian Learning-Enhanced Navigation with Deep Smoothing for Inertial-Aided Navigation
summary: Accurate post-processing navigation is essential for applications such as survey and mapping, where the full measurement history can be exploited to refine past state estimates. Fixed-interval smoothing algorithms represent the theoretically optimal solution under Gaussian assumptions. However, loosely coupled INS/GNSS systems fundamentally inherit the systematic position bias of raw GNSS measurements, leaving a persistent accuracy gap that model-based smoothers cannot resolve. To address this limitation, we propose BLENDS, which integrates Bayesian learning with deep smoothing to enhance navigation performance. BLENDS is a a data-driven post-processing framework that augments the classical two-filter smoother with a transformer-based neural network. It learns to modify the filter covariance matrices and apply an additive correction to the smoothed error-state directly within the Bayesian framework. A novel Bayesian-consistent loss jointly supervises the smoothed mean and covariance, enforcing minimum-variance estimates while maintaining statistical consistency. BLENDS is evaluated on two real-world datasets spanning a mobile robot and a quadrotor. Across all unseen test trajectories, BLENDS achieves horizontal position improvements of up to 63% over the baseline forward EKF.

AI.tldr: BLENDS is a data-driven post-processing navigation framework that integrates Bayesian learning with deep smoothing using a transformer-based neural network to modify filter covariances and correct smoothed error-states, achieving up to 63% horizontal position improvement over baseline EKF.
AI.motivation: Accurate post-processing navigation is essential for survey and mapping applications. While fixed-interval smoothing algorithms are theoretically optimal under Gaussian assumptions, loosely coupled INS/GNSS systems suffer from systematic position bias in raw GNSS measurements, leaving a persistent accuracy gap that model-based smoothers cannot resolve.
AI.method: BLENDS augments the classical two-filter smoother with a transformer-based neural network that learns to modify filter covariance matrices and apply additive corrections to smoothed error-states within a Bayesian framework. It employs a novel Bayesian-consistent loss function that jointly supervises the smoothed mean and covariance, enforcing minimum-variance estimates while maintaining statistical consistency.
AI.result: Evaluated on two real-world datasets spanning a mobile robot and a quadrotor, BLENDS achieves horizontal position improvements of up to 63% over the baseline forward EKF across all unseen test trajectories.
AI.conclusion: BLENDS effectively addresses the systematic bias limitation of model-based smoothers by combining Bayesian learning with deep smoothing, demonstrating significant performance improvements in post-processing navigation accuracy.

title: Integrating Deep RL and Bayesian Inference for ObjectNav in Mobile Robotics
comment: Accepted and to be published in the ICARSC 2026 26th IEEE International Conference on Autonomous Robot Systems and Competitions
summary: Autonomous object search is challenging for mobile robots operating in indoor environments due to partial observability, perceptual uncertainty, and the need to trade off exploration and navigation efficiency. Classical probabilistic approaches explicitly represent uncertainty but typically rely on handcrafted action-selection heuristics, while deep reinforcement learning enables adaptive policies but often suffers from slow convergence and limited interpretability. This paper proposes a hybrid object-search framework that integrates Bayesian inference with deep reinforcement learning. The method maintains a spatial belief map over target locations, updated online through Bayesian inference from calibrated object detections, and trains a reinforcement learning policy to select navigation actions directly from this probabilistic representation. The approach is evaluated in realistic indoor simulation using Habitat 3.0 and compared against developed baseline strategies. Across two indoor environments, the proposed method improves success rate while reducing search effort. Overall, the results support the value of combining Bayesian belief estimation with learned action selection to achieve more efficient and reliable objectsearch behavior under partial observability.

AI.tldr: A hybrid framework combining Bayesian inference with deep reinforcement learning for efficient autonomous object search in indoor environments under partial observability.
AI.motivation: Autonomous object search is challenging due to partial observability, perceptual uncertainty, and the need to balance exploration and navigation efficiency. Classical probabilistic approaches rely on handcrafted action-selection heuristics, while deep reinforcement learning suffers from slow convergence and limited interpretability.
AI.method: The method maintains a spatial belief map over target locations, updated online through Bayesian inference from calibrated object detections. A reinforcement learning policy is trained to select navigation actions directly from this probabilistic representation, integrating Bayesian estimation with learned action selection.
AI.result: Evaluated in realistic indoor simulation using Habitat 3.0 across two environments. The proposed method improves success rate while reducing search effort compared to baseline strategies.
AI.conclusion: Combining Bayesian belief estimation with learned action selection achieves more efficient and reliable object search behavior under partial observability, demonstrating the value of hybrid approaches that leverage both probabilistic reasoning and learned policies.

title: IntentReact: Guiding Reactive Object-Centric Navigation via Topological Intent
summary: Object-goal visual navigation requires robots to reason over semantic structure and act effectively under partial observability. Recent approaches based on object-level topological maps enable long-horizon navigation without dense geometric reconstruction, but their execution remains limited by the gap between global topological guidance and local perception-driven control. In particular, local decisions are made solely from the current egocentric observation, without access to information beyond the robot's field of view. As a result, the robot may persist along its current heading even when initially oriented away from the goal, moving toward directions that do not decrease the global topological distance. In this work, we propose IntentReact, an intent-conditioned object-centric navigation framework that introduces a compact interface between global topological planning and reactive object-centric control. Our approach encodes global topological guidance as a low-dimensional directional signal, termed intent, which conditions a learned waypoint prediction policy to bias navigation toward topologically consistent progression. This design enables the robot to promptly reorient when local observations are misleading, guiding motion toward directions that decrease global topological distance while preserving the reactivity and robustness of object-centric control. We evaluate the proposed framework through extensive experiments, demonstrating improved navigation success and execution quality compared to prior object-centric navigation methods.

AI.tldr: IntentReact introduces an intent-conditioned object-centric navigation framework that bridges global topological guidance and local perception-driven control by encoding topological information as a low-dimensional directional signal to bias waypoint prediction policies.
AI.motivation: Object-goal visual navigation requires reasoning over semantic structure and handling partial observability. Recent object-level topological maps enable long-horizon navigation but suffer from a gap between global topological guidance and local perception-driven control. Local decisions are made solely from the current egocentric observation without access to information beyond the field of view, causing the robot to persist along its current heading even when initially oriented away from the goal.
AI.method: IntentReact encodes global topological guidance as a low-dimensional directional signal called "intent" that conditions a learned waypoint prediction policy. This intent signal biases navigation toward topologically consistent progression, enabling the robot to promptly reorient when local observations are misleading while preserving the reactivity and robustness of object-centric control.
AI.result: Extensive experiments demonstrate improved navigation success and execution quality compared to prior object-centric navigation methods.
AI.conclusion: The framework enables the robot to guide motion toward directions that decrease global topological distance while preserving the reactivity and robustness of object-centric control, successfully bridging the gap between global topological planning and local perception-driven control.

title: MMaDA-VLA: Large Diffusion Vision-Language-Action Model with Unified Multi-Modal Instruction and Generation
summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models aim to control robots for manipulation from visual observations and natural-language instructions. However, existing hierarchical and autoregressive paradigms often introduce architectural overhead, suffer from temporal inconsistency and long-horizon error accumulation, and lack a mechanism to capture environment dynamics without extra modules. To this end, we present MMaDA-VLA, a fully native pre-trained large diffusion VLA model that unifies multi-modal understanding and generation in a single framework. Our key idea is a native discrete diffusion formulation that embeds language, images, and continuous robot controls into one discrete token space and trains a single backbone with masked token denoising to jointly generate a future goal observation and an action chunk in parallel. Iterative denoising enables global, order-free refinement, improving long-horizon consistency while grounding actions in predicted future visual outcomes without auxiliary world models. Experiments across simulation benchmarks and real-world tasks show state-of-the-art performance, achieving 98.0% average success on LIBERO and 4.78 average length on CALVIN.

AI.tldr: MMaDA-VLA is a large diffusion VLA model that unifies multi-modal understanding and generation in a single framework using a native discrete diffusion formulation, enabling joint generation of future goal observations and action chunks through iterative denoising.
AI.motivation: Existing hierarchical and autoregressive VLA models suffer from architectural overhead, temporal inconsistency, long-horizon error accumulation, and lack mechanisms to capture environment dynamics without extra modules.
AI.method: MMaDA-VLA uses a native discrete diffusion formulation that embeds language, images, and continuous robot controls into one discrete token space. A single backbone is trained with masked token denoising to jointly generate a future goal observation and an action chunk in parallel. Iterative denoising enables global, order-free refinement.
AI.result: Achieved state-of-the-art performance with 98.0% average success rate on LIBERO and 4.78 average length on CALVIN.
AI.conclusion: The iterative denoising approach improves long-horizon consistency while grounding actions in predicted future visual outcomes without requiring auxiliary world models.

title: Visualizing Impedance Control in Augmented Reality for Teleoperation: Design and User Evaluation
comment: 6 pages, 5 figures, submitted to IEEE RO-MAN 2026
summary: Teleoperation for contact-rich manipulation remains challenging, especially when using low-cost, motion-only interfaces that provide no haptic feedback. Virtual reality controllers enable intuitive motion control but do not allow operators to directly perceive or regulate contact forces, limiting task performance. To address this, we propose an augmented reality (AR) visualization of the impedance controller's target pose and its displacement from each robot end effector. This visualization conveys the forces generated by the controller, providing operators with intuitive, real-time feedback without expensive haptic hardware. We evaluate the design in a dual-arm manipulation study with 17 participants who repeatedly reposition a box with and without the AR visualization. Results show that AR visualization reduces completion time by 24% for force-critical lifting tasks, with no significant effect on sliding tasks where precise force control is less critical. These findings indicate that making the impedance target visible through AR is a viable approach to improve human-robot interaction for contact-rich teleoperation.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes an augmented reality (AR) visualization that displays the impedance controller's target pose and its displacement from the robot's end effector, allowing operators to intuitively perceive contact forces without expensive haptic hardware. In a dual-arm manipulation study with 17 participants, AR visualization reduced task completion time by 24% for force-critical lifting tasks, demonstrating its effectiveness for contact-rich teleoperation.
AI.motivation: Teleoperation for contact-rich manipulation is challenging, especially when using low-cost, motion-only interfaces that lack haptic feedback. Virtual reality controllers enable intuitive motion control but do not allow operators to directly perceive or regulate contact forces, limiting task performance.
AI.method: The researchers proposed an augmented reality (AR) visualization that displays the impedance controller's target pose and its displacement from each robot's end effector. This visualization conveys the forces generated by the controller, providing operators with intuitive, real-time feedback without requiring expensive haptic hardware. The study was conducted with 17 participants in a dual-arm manipulation experiment, where they repeatedly repositioned a box with and without the AR visualization.
AI.result: AR visualization reduced task completion time by 24% for force-critical lifting tasks, while having no significant effect on sliding tasks where precise force control was less critical.
AI.conclusion: Making the impedance target visible through AR is a viable approach to improve human-robot interaction for contact-rich teleoperation, especially for tasks that require force control.

title: LILAC: Language-Conditioned Object-Centric Optical Flow for Open-Loop Trajectory Generation
summary: We address language-conditioned robotic manipulation using flow-based trajectory generation, which enables training on human and web videos of object manipulation and requires only minimal embodiment-specific data. This task is challenging, as object trajectory generation from pre-manipulation images and natural language instructions requires appropriate instruction-flow alignment. To tackle this challenge, we propose the flow-based Language Instruction-guided open-Loop ACtion generator (LILAC). This flow-based Vision-Language-Action model (VLA) generates object-centric 2D optical flow from an RGB image and a natural language instruction, and converts the flow into a 6-DoF manipulator trajectory. LILAC incorporates two key components: Semantic Alignment Loss, which strengthens language conditioning to generate instruction-aligned optical flow, and Prompt-Conditioned Cross-Modal Adapter, which aligns learned visual prompts with image and text features to provide rich cues for flow generation. Experimentally, our method outperformed existing approaches in generated flow quality across multiple benchmarks. Furthermore, in physical object manipulation experiments using free-form instructions, LILAC demonstrated a superior task success rate compared to existing methods. The project page is available at https://lilac-75srg.kinsta.page/.

AI.tldr: LILAC is a flow-based Vision-Language-Action model that generates 6-DoF manipulator trajectories from RGB images and natural language instructions for language-conditioned robotic manipulation.
AI.motivation: Language-conditioned robotic manipulation is challenging because generating object trajectories from pre-manipulation images and natural language instructions requires appropriate instruction-flow alignment. Existing approaches typically require substantial embodiment-specific data for training.
AI.method: LILAC generates object-centric 2D optical flow from RGB images and natural language instructions, then converts the flow into 6-DoF manipulator trajectories. Key components include: (1) Semantic Alignment Loss to strengthen language conditioning for instruction-aligned flow generation, and (2) Prompt-Conditioned Cross-Modal Adapter to align learned visual prompts with image and text features for richer flow generation cues.
AI.result: LILAC outperformed existing approaches in generated flow quality across multiple benchmarks and achieved superior task success rate in physical object manipulation experiments using free-form instructions.
AI.conclusion: The proposed method effectively addresses the instruction-flow alignment challenge, enabling training on human and web videos with minimal embodiment-specific data, demonstrating that flow-based trajectory generation can achieve state-of-the-art performance in language-conditioned robotic manipulation tasks.

title: Towards Generalizable Robotic Data Flywheel: High-Dimensional Factorization and Composition
summary: The lack of sufficiently diverse data, coupled with limited data efficiency, remains a major bottleneck for generalist robotic models, yet systematic strategies for collecting and curating such data are not fully explored. Task diversity arises from implicit factors that are sparsely distributed across multiple dimensions and are difficult to define explicitly. To address this challenge, we propose F-ACIL, a heuristic factor-aware compositional iterative learning framework that enables structured data factorization and promotes compositional generalization. F-ACIL decomposes the data distribution into structured factor spaces such as object, action, and environment. Based on the factorized formulation, we develop a factor-wise data collection and an iterative training paradigm that promotes compositional generalization over the high-dimensional factor space, leading to more effective utilization of real-world robotic demonstrations. With extensive real-world experiments, we show that F-ACIL can achieve more than 45% performance gains with 5-10$\times$ fewer demonstrations comparing to that of which without the strategy. The results suggest that structured factorization offers a practical pathway toward efficient compositional generalization in real-world robotic learning. We believe F-ACIL can inspire more systematic research on building generalizable robotic data flywheel strategies. More demonstrations can be found at: https://f-acil.github.io/

AI.tldr: F-ACIL is a heuristic factor-aware compositional iterative learning framework that enables structured data factorization into object, action, and environment factor spaces, promoting compositional generalization for robotic models with 45%+ performance gains using 5-10× fewer demonstrations.
AI.motivation: The lack of sufficiently diverse data and limited data efficiency remain major bottlenecks for generalist robotic models. Task diversity arises from implicit factors that are sparsely distributed across multiple dimensions and are difficult to define explicitly, making systematic strategies for collecting and curating diverse data challenging.
AI.method: F-ACIL decomposes the data distribution into structured factor spaces (object, action, environment). Based on this factorized formulation, it develops a factor-wise data collection strategy and an iterative training paradigm that promotes compositional generalization over the high-dimensional factor space, enabling more effective utilization of real-world robotic demonstrations.
AI.result: Extensive real-world experiments demonstrate that F-ACIL achieves more than 45% performance gains while requiring only 5-10× fewer demonstrations compared to the baseline without the proposed strategy.
AI.conclusion: Structured factorization offers a practical pathway toward efficient compositional generalization in real-world robotic learning. F-ACIL can inspire more systematic research on building generalizable robotic data flywheel strategies, enabling more effective utilization of real-world robotic demonstrations.

title: Accurate Surface and Reflectance Modelling from 3D Radar Data with Neural Radiance Fields
summary: Robust scene representation is essential for autonomous systems to safely operate in challenging low-visibility environments. Radar has a clear advantage over cameras and lidars in these conditions due to its resilience to environmental factors such as fog, smoke, or dust. However, radar data is inherently sparse and noisy, making reliable 3D surface reconstruction challenging. To address these challenges, we propose a neural implicit approach for 3D mapping from radar point clouds, which jointly models scene geometry and view-dependent radar intensities. Our method leverages a memory-efficient hybrid feature encoding to learn a continuous Signed Distance Field (SDF) for surface reconstruction, while also capturing radar-specific reflective properties. We show that our approach produces smoother, more accurate 3D surface reconstructions compared to existing lidar-based reconstruction methods applied to radar data, and can reconstruct view-dependent radar intensities. We also show that in general, as input point clouds get sparser, neural implicit representations render more faithful surfaces, compared to traditional explicit SDFs and meshing techniques.

AI.tldr: A neural implicit approach for 3D mapping from radar point clouds that jointly models scene geometry and view-dependent radar intensities using a memory-efficient hybrid feature encoding to learn a continuous SDF for surface reconstruction.
AI.motivation: Robust scene representation is critical for autonomous systems operating in low-visibility environments. While radar excels over cameras and lidars in conditions like fog, smoke, and dust due to its environmental resilience, radar data is inherently sparse and noisy, making reliable 3D surface reconstruction challenging.
AI.method: The paper proposes a neural implicit approach for 3D mapping from radar point clouds that jointly models scene geometry and view-dependent radar intensities. The method leverages a memory-efficient hybrid feature encoding to learn a continuous Signed Distance Field (SDF) for surface reconstruction while capturing radar-specific reflective properties.
AI.result: The approach produces smoother, more accurate 3D surface reconstructions compared to existing lidar-based reconstruction methods applied to radar data and can reconstruct view-dependent radar intensities. Additionally, neural implicit representations render more faithful surfaces than traditional explicit SDFs and meshing techniques, especially as input point clouds become sparser.
AI.conclusion: The proposed method effectively addresses the challenges of sparse and noisy radar data for 3D surface reconstruction, outperforming traditional approaches and being particularly advantageous for low-visibility scenarios where radar is the primary sensing modality.

title: A Mentalistic Interface for Probing Folk-Psychological Attribution to Non-Humanoid Robots
comment: Preprint submitted to IEEE. 8 pages, 21 figures
summary: This paper presents an experimental platform for studying intentional-state attribution toward a non-humanoid robot. The system combines a simulated robot, realistic task environments, and large language model-based explanatory layers that can express the same behavior in mentalistic, teleological, or mechanistic terms. By holding behavior constant while varying the explanatory frame, the platform provides a controlled way to investigate how language and framing shape the adoption of the intentional stance in robotics.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces an experimental platform combining a simulated robot, realistic task environments, and LLM-based explanatory layers to systematically investigate how language and framing affect the adoption of the intentional stance toward non-humanoid robots.
AI.motivation: The authors aim to understand how linguistic framing (mentalistic, teleological, or mechanistic explanations) influences human attribution of intentional states to robots, a key question in human-robot interaction and the theory of the intentional stance.
AI.method: The platform integrates a simulated non-humanoid robot operating in realistic task environments with large language model-based explanatory layers that can generate behavior descriptions using mentalistic, teleological, or mechanistic framing. The experimental design holds robot behavior constant while systematically varying the explanatory frame presented to participants.
AI.result: The platform provides a controlled experimental setup to examine the causal relationship between language framing and intentional stance adoption, enabling precise measurement of how different explanatory styles influence human interpretations of robot actions.
AI.conclusion: By decoupling behavior from explanation through this platform, researchers can isolate the effects of linguistic framing on intentional-state attribution, offering new insights into how humans construct mental models of artificial agents and the implications for human-robot interaction design.

title: Fast-dVLA: Accelerating Discrete Diffusion VLA to Real-Time Performance
summary: This paper proposes a novel approach to address the challenge that pretrained VLA models often fail to effectively improve performance and reduce adaptation costs during standard supervised finetuning (SFT). Some advanced finetuning methods with auxiliary training objectives can improve performance and reduce the number of convergence steps. However, they typically incur significant computational overhead due to the additional losses from auxiliary tasks. To simultaneously achieve the enhanced capabilities of auxiliary training with the simplicity of standard SFT, we decouple the two objectives of auxiliary task training within the parameter space, namely, enhancing general capabilities and fitting task-specific action distributions. To deliver this goal, we only need to train the model to converge on a small-scale task set using two distinct training strategies. The difference between the resulting model parameters can then be interpreted as capability vectors provided by auxiliary tasks. These vectors are then merged with pretrained parameters to form a capability-enhanced meta model. Moreover, when standard SFT is augmented with a lightweight orthogonal regularization loss, the merged model attains performance comparable to auxiliary finetuned baselines with reduced computational overhead. Experimental results demonstrate that this approach is highly effective across diverse robot tasks. Project page: https://chris1220313648.github.io/Fast-dVLA/

AI.tldr: A novel approach that decouples auxiliary task training objectives within parameter space to enhance pretrained VLA models, enabling performance comparable to auxiliary finetuning baselines with significantly reduced computational overhead during standard SFT.
AI.motivation: Pretrained VLA models often fail to effectively improve performance and reduce adaptation costs during standard supervised finetuning (SFT). While advanced finetuning methods with auxiliary training objectives can improve performance and reduce convergence steps, they typically incur significant computational overhead due to additional losses from auxiliary tasks.
AI.method: The method decouples the two objectives of auxiliary task training within parameter space: enhancing general capabilities and fitting task-specific action distributions. It trains the model on a small-scale task set using two distinct training strategies, where the difference between resulting parameters represents capability vectors from auxiliary tasks. These vectors are merged with pretrained parameters to form a capability-enhanced meta model. When augmenting standard SFT with a lightweight orthogonal regularization loss, the merged model achieves the desired performance improvement.
AI.result: The merged model attains performance comparable to auxiliary finetuned baselines with reduced computational overhead. The approach is highly effective across diverse robot tasks, demonstrating that it can simultaneously achieve the enhanced capabilities of auxiliary training with the simplicity of standard SFT.
AI.conclusion: By decoupling auxiliary training objectives in parameter space and using lightweight orthogonal regularization, this approach successfully combines the performance benefits of auxiliary training with the computational efficiency of standard SFT, making it a practical solution for enhancing VLA models in robotics applications.

title: Can Users Specify Driving Speed? Bench2Drive-Speed: Benchmark and Baselines for Desired-Speed Conditioned Autonomous Driving
summary: End-to-end autonomous driving (E2E-AD) has achieved remarkable progress. However, one practical and useful function has been long overlooked: users may wish to customize the desired speed of the policy or specify whether to allow the autonomous vehicle to overtake. To bridge this gap, we present Bench2Drive-Speed, a benchmark with metrics, dataset, and baselines for desired-speed conditioned autonomous driving. We introduce explicit inputs of users' desired target-speed and overtake/follow instructions to driving policy models. We design quantitative metrics, including Speed-Adherence Score and Overtake Score, to measure how faithfully policies follow user specifications, while remaining compatible with standard autonomous driving metrics. To enable training of speed-conditioned policies, one approach is to collect expert demonstrations that strictly follow speed requirements, an expensive and unscalable process in the real world. An alternative is to adapt existing regular driving data by treating the speed observed in future frames as the target speed for training. To investigate this, we construct CustomizedSpeedDataset, composed of 2,100 clips annotated with experts demonstrations, enabling systematic investigation of supervision strategies. Our experiments show that, under proper re-annotation, models trained on regular driving data perform comparably to on expert demonstrations, suggesting that speed supervision can be introduced without additional complex real-world data collection. Furthermore, we find that while target-speed following can be achieved without degrading regular driving performance, executing overtaking commands remains challenging due to the inherent difficulty of interactive behaviors. All code, datasets and baselines are available at https://github.com/Thinklab-SJTU/Bench2Drive-Speed

AI.tldr: Bench2Drive-Speed is a benchmark for desired-speed conditioned autonomous driving, introducing explicit speed and overtaking instructions as inputs to driving policies, along with Speed-Adherence and Overtake scores to measure compliance.
AI.motivation: While end-to-end autonomous driving has advanced, users' ability to customize driving behaviors—such as specifying desired speeds or allowing overtaking—has been overlooked. This gap needs to be bridged to make autonomous vehicles more user-centric.
AI.method: 1) Introduced explicit inputs for target-speed and overtaking/following instructions to driving policy models. 2) Designed quantitative metrics: Speed-Adherence Score and Overtake Score. 3) Created CustomizedSpeedDataset with 2,100 expert-annotated clips. 4) Investigated supervision strategies, comparing expert demonstrations vs. adapting regular driving data by treating future speeds as targets.
AI.result: Models trained on regular driving data with proper re-annotation achieve performance comparable to expert demonstrations for speed following. Speed-Adherence can be achieved without degrading regular driving performance. Overtaking commands remain challenging due to the inherent difficulty of interactive behaviors.
AI.conclusion: Speed supervision can be introduced to autonomous driving policies without additional complex real-world data collection by properly re-annotating existing data, though overtaking remains a challenging task requiring further research.

title: Persistent Robot World Models: Stabilizing Multi-Step Rollouts via Reinforcement Learning
summary: Action-conditioned robot world models generate future video frames of the manipulated scene given a robot action sequence, offering a promising alternative for simulating tasks that are difficult to model with traditional physics engines. However, these models are optimized for short-term prediction and break down when deployed autoregressively: each predicted clip feeds back as context for the next, causing errors to compound and visual quality to rapidly degrade. We address this through the following contributions. First, we introduce a reinforcement learning (RL) post-training scheme that trains the world model on its own autoregressive rollouts rather than on ground-truth histories. We achieve this by adapting a recent contrastive RL objective for diffusion models to our setting and show that its convergence guarantees carry over exactly. Second, we design a training protocol that generates and compares multiple candidate variable-length futures from the same rollout state, reinforcing higher-fidelity predictions over lower-fidelity ones. Third, we develop efficient, multi-view visual fidelity rewards that combine complementary perceptual metrics across camera views and are aggregated at the clip level for dense, low-variance training signal. Fourth, we show that our approach establishes a new state-of-the-art for rollout fidelity on the DROID dataset, outperforming the strongest baseline on all metrics (e.g., LPIPS reduced by 14% on external cameras, SSIM improved by 9.1% on the wrist camera), winning 98% of paired comparisons, and achieving an 80% preference rate in a blind human study.

AI.tldr: A reinforcement learning post-training scheme for action-conditioned robot world models that improves long-horizon autoregressive rollout fidelity through contrastive training on generated futures, multi-view perceptual rewards, and variable-length comparison protocols, achieving state-of-the-art performance on DROID dataset with 98% paired comparison wins and 80% human preference rate.
AI.motivation: Action-conditioned robot world models optimized for short-term prediction fail when deployed autoregressively due to error compounding and visual quality degradation in long-horizon rollout generation.
AI.method: Four key innovations: (1) RL post-training scheme adapting contrastive RL objective for diffusion models to train on autoregressive rollouts; (2) Protocol generating and comparing multiple variable-length candidate futures; (3) Multi-view visual fidelity rewards combining perceptual metrics; (4) Clip-level aggregation for dense training signal.
AI.result: Achieves new SOTA on DROID dataset: LPIPS reduced by 14% on external cameras, SSIM improved by 9.1% on wrist camera, winning 98% of paired comparisons and achieving 80% preference rate in blind human study.
AI.conclusion: The proposed approach effectively addresses the error compounding problem in autoregressive robot world models, establishing a new benchmark for rollout fidelity and demonstrating strong perceptual quality improvements through novel training methodologies.

title: Intelligent Navigation and Obstacle-Aware Fabrication for Mobile Additive Manufacturing Systems
summary: As the demand for mass customization increases, manufacturing systems must become more flexible and adaptable to produce personalized products efficiently. Additive manufacturing (AM) enhances production adaptability by enabling on-demand fabrication of customized components directly from digital models, but its flexibility remains constrained by fixed equipment layouts. Integrating mobile robots addresses this limitation by allowing manufacturing resources to move and adapt to changing production requirements. Mobile AM Robots (MAMbots) combine AM with mobile robotics to produce and transport components within dynamic manufacturing environments. However, the dynamic manufacturing environments introduce challenges for MAMbots. Disturbances such as obstacles and uneven terrain can disrupt navigation stability, which in turn affects printing accuracy and surface quality. This work proposes a universal mobile printing-and-delivery platform that couples navigation and material deposition, addressing the limitations of earlier frameworks that treated these processes separately. A real-time control framework is developed to plan and control the robot's navigation, ensuring safe motion, obstacle avoidance, and path stability while maintaining print quality. The closed-loop integration of sensing, mobility, and manufacturing provides real-time feedback for motion and process control, enabling MAMbots to make autonomous decisions in dynamic environments. The framework is validated through simulations and real-world experiments that test its adaptability to trajectory variations and external disturbances. Coupled navigation and printing together enable MAMbots to plan safe, adaptive trajectories, improving flexibility and adaptability in manufacturing.

AI.tldr: A universal mobile printing-and-delivery platform integrating navigation and material deposition for Mobile AM Robots (MAMbots), enabling autonomous decision-making in dynamic manufacturing environments through a real-time control framework.
AI.motivation: The paper addresses the limitations of additive manufacturing (AM) constrained by fixed equipment layouts. With increasing demand for mass customization, manufacturing systems require greater flexibility. While mobile robots can address this limitation, disturbances (obstacles, uneven terrain) disrupt navigation stability, affecting printing accuracy and surface quality. Earlier frameworks treated navigation and printing separately, limiting overall system adaptability.
AI.method: A real-time control framework was developed to plan and control robot navigation, ensuring safe motion, obstacle avoidance, and path stability while maintaining print quality. The approach features closed-loop integration of sensing, mobility, and manufacturing, providing real-time feedback for motion and process control. The platform couples navigation and material deposition processes, validated through simulations and real-world experiments testing adaptability to trajectory variations and external disturbances.
AI.result: The coupled navigation and printing approach enables MAMbots to plan safe, adaptive trajectories, improving flexibility and adaptability in manufacturing. The framework successfully addresses the limitations of earlier separate-process frameworks and allows autonomous decision-making in dynamic environments.
AI.conclusion: Integrating navigation and material deposition through a real-time control framework provides a superior solution for Mobile AM Robots, overcoming the constraints of fixed equipment layouts and enabling efficient production of personalized products in dynamic manufacturing environments.

title: SoftMimicGen: A Data Generation System for Scalable Robot Learning in Deformable Object Manipulation
summary: Large-scale robot datasets have facilitated the learning of a wide range of robot manipulation skills, but these datasets remain difficult to collect and scale further, owing to the intractable amount of human time, effort, and cost required. Simulation and synthetic data generation have proven to be an effective alternative to fuel this need for data, especially with the advent of recent work showing that such synthetic datasets can dramatically reduce real-world data requirements and facilitate generalization to novel scenarios unseen in real-world demonstrations. However, this paradigm has been limited to rigid-body tasks, which are easy to simulate. Deformable object manipulation encompasses a large portion of real-world manipulation and remains a crucial gap to address towards increasing adoption of the synthetic simulation data paradigm. In this paper, we introduce SoftMimicGen, an automated data generation pipeline for deformable object manipulation tasks. We introduce a suite of high-fidelity simulation environments that encompasses a wide range of deformable objects (stuffed animal, rope, tissue, towel) and manipulation behaviors (high-precision threading, dynamic whipping, folding, pick-and-place), across four robot embodiments: a single-arm manipulator, bimanual arms, a humanoid, and a surgical robot. We apply SoftMimicGen to generate datasets across the task suite, train high-performing policies from the data, and systematically analyze the data generation system. Project website: \href{https://softmimicgen.github.io}{softmimicgen.github.io}.

AI.tldr: SoftMimicGen introduces an automated data generation pipeline for deformable object manipulation tasks, using high-fidelity simulation across various objects, robot embodiments, and manipulation behaviors to enable policy training without extensive real-world data collection.
AI.motivation: Large-scale robot datasets are difficult and costly to collect in the real world, while current synthetic simulation approaches are limited to rigid-body tasks and cannot handle deformable object manipulation, which represents a significant portion of real-world manipulation tasks.
AI.method: SoftMimicGen creates a suite of high-fidelity simulation environments featuring various deformable objects (stuffed animal, rope, tissue, towel) and manipulation behaviors (threading, whipping, folding, pick-and-place) across four robot embodiments (single-arm, bimanual, humanoid, surgical robot) to generate synthetic datasets for training robot policies.
AI.result: The authors applied SoftMimicGen to generate datasets across the task suite, trained high-performing policies from this data, and systematically analyzed the data generation system to demonstrate its effectiveness.
AI.conclusion: SoftMimicGen effectively addresses the gap in deformable object manipulation simulation, enabling scalable data generation that can reduce real-world data requirements and facilitate generalization to novel scenarios.
